summary: Edward Albert Gait was an Indologist and historian who studied at University College London from around 1880 to 1882. He founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Amundsen was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He served with the Tibetan Pioneer Mission in 1893, was Superintendent for South-West China and Tibet for the British and Foreign Bible Society (1903–1915), and served at Det Norske Misjonsforbund (1919–1924).

Edward Arthur Henry Blunt worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Marlborough College, Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and University College London. He joined the Indian Civil Service (1901) and served as Financial Secretary to the United Provinces (1920–1931).

Edward Backhouse Eastwick was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Charterhouse, Merton College, and Oxford, he was Professor of Hindustani and Telugu (1845) and librarian (1850) at East India Company College.

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Magdalen Hall under Horace Hayman Wilson. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian studies, he was Principal of Sanskrit College (1858–1864) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge from 1867 to 1903.

Edward C. Dimock Jr., an Indologist and linguist, earned degrees from Yale and Harvard, completing his Ph.D. under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at the University of Chicago (1959–1993) and presided over the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

Edward Capps was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).

Edward Clive Bayley worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at the East India Company College. He joined the Indian Civil Service in 1842, later serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1869–1874) and President of The Asiatic Society (c. 1873–1878).

Edward Conze was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied across German universities, including Cologne under Max Scheler. He held posts at the University of London (c. 1933–1960) and the University of Washington (1965–1968), alongside several visiting professorships.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University and under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen. He served as a professor and Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy at Columbia University (1880–1931).

Edward Denison Ross was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies scholar. Educated at UCL and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke, he served as Principal of Aliah University (1901) and Administrator and Professor of Persian at SOAS (1916–1937).

Edward Douglas Maclagan was an Indologist and historian educated at Winchester College and New College, Oxford. He served as Chancellor of the University of the Punjab from 1919 to 1924 and as President of the Royal Asiatic Society from 1925 to 1928.

Edward Edwards specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Bala Theological College, Aberystwyth under Hermann Ethé, and Christ's College, Cambridge. He worked as an Assistant at the British Museum from 1904 to 1935.

Edward Elbridge Salisbury was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale and in Europe under Eugène Burnouf and Franz Bopp. He was Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854) and later served as President of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard was a religious studies scholar who studied at Oxford and at the London School of Economics under Bronisław Malinowski. He held academic posts at Cairo University, Cambridge, and served as professor at the University of Oxford (1946–1970).
Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is an Indology, Buddhist, and religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell. He held an academic post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche. He worked as a researcher at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Geoffrey Parrinder was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Richmond College. He served as Senior Lecturer at the University of Ibadan from around 1949 to 1953 and became Reader at King's College London in 1958.

Edward Granville Browne specialized in Iranian studies and linguistics, studying at Pembroke College, Cambridge, under Edward Byles Cowell. He served Cambridge as Lecturer in Persian (1888) and Adams Professor of Arabic (1902), and became a Fellow of the British Academy (1903).

Edward Green Balfour was an Indologist educated at Montrose Academy and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (founded 1850), founded the Mysore Museum in 1866, and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.
